findings.reason: CAP0_PASS 2026-11-20 on the Windows host: Git, Windows/WSL2, rootless Podman machine, PostgreSQL 17.5 + PostGIS 3.5.2 healthy via podman compose, SRID 32643 present, image digest resolved, Cargo.lock and pnpm-lock.yaml generated by host tools, cargo check --workspace --locked exit 0, pnpm frozen install and web build exit 0, validate_package.py exit 0 (--release EXPECTED_FAIL on 6 placeholder specs). Not a release approval; P-13 and P-14 remain open. See audit/CAP0_REPORT.md.

No .git existed in the canonical folder or any parent (git rev-parse exit 128). Initialised exactly at C:/Projects/Mumbai Civic Lens/mumbai-civic-lens on branch main; as-found pre-CAP-0 baseline is commit 099f36b. .env.local is ignored (.gitignore:1) and untracked.

docs/reference/MUMBAI_CIVIC_LENS_MASTER_REFERENCE_GUIDE.md is user-supplied, historical v1.2.2 background and non-authoritative. The v1.2.3 validator requires every physical file to be manifested and its exclusions were not weakened, so the file is retained and hash-pinned in PACKAGE_MANIFEST.json with required=false (supplementary). Sandbox-era claim that this was a plain 'resolved' correction was re-derived on the host.

Cargo.lock and pnpm-lock.yaml are not in the validator exclusion list, so they must be manifested. Both were generated by the real host package managers (cargo 1.85.0, pnpm 11.28.9) and added to PACKAGE_MANIFEST.json with real hashes; validator unchanged.

Podman machine could not start on WSL 2.3.24.0 (systemd 259 needs cgroup v2; then no WSL network interface). After the user updated WSL to 3.0.5.0 (kernel 6.18) the machine runs rootless on cgroup v2. Mirrored networking still produced no interface, so ~/.wslconfig networkingMode was set to nat (user-approved; WSL fell back to Consomme) and Windows can reach WSL ports (ssh 52664, DB 5432). Original ~/.wslconfig kept at ~/.wslconfig.bak-cap0-20261120162547; the nat edit is backed up as ~/.wslconfig.bak-cap0-b-*. See CAP0-F08 for the remaining workarounds.

Host rustc is 1.85.0; unconstrained resolution picks crates needing rustc 1.88-1.89 (time, uuid, icu_*), so cargo check failed (exit 101). Toolchain was not changed; Cargo.lock was generated with CARGO_RESOLVER_INCOMPATIBLE_RUST_VERSIONS=fallback (axum 0.8.9, sqlx 0.8.6, time 0.3.45, uuid 1.26.1). Also https://index.crates.io returns HTTP 403 via the corporate proxy, so cargo needs CARGO_REGISTRIES_CRATES_IO_PROTOCOL=git on this host. Residual risk: later dependency bumps need a newer toolchain decision.

'tsc -b' in the web build emitted apps/web/src/main.js and apps/web/tsconfig.tsbuildinfo into the manifested tree, making the validator fail (unmanifested). Bounded fix in apps/web/tsconfig.json: noEmit=true and tsBuildInfoFile under node_modules/.tmp. Rebuild emits nothing outside dist/.

pnpm 11 fails installs with ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS for esbuild@0.25.12. Explicitly denied via 'pnpm approve-builds !esbuild' (allowBuilds: esbuild: false in pnpm-workspace.yaml); the production build and frozen install pass without the script.

Host workarounds needed to run the DB with Podman on this machine, none stored in the repo: (1) podman.exe is not on PATH (user Programs/Podman folder) and its default provider is hyperv, so CONTAINERS_MACHINE_PROVIDER=wsl; (2) win-sshproxy failed to bind its unix socket under the 8.3 short TEMP path (HEMANT~1.BHA), so TEMP/TMP were pointed at C:/Users/<LOCAL_USER>/pmtmp and a stale unremovable Temp/podman folder was renamed to podman.stale-cap0; (3) Docker Compose (default provider) cannot reach the machine's named pipe, so PODMAN_COMPOSE_PROVIDER points at podman-compose 1.6.0 in a venv outside the repo (C:/Users/<LOCAL_USER>/pmtmp/venv); (4) the corporate TLS-inspection root (Zscaler Root CA, already trusted by Windows) was added to the Podman VM trust store so image pulls verify; (5) 'podman machine start' returns exit 125 (ssh handshake reset) although the machine reaches Currently running. A bootstrap script for these is future work. P1 addition: on this host 'localhost' resolves to ::1 first and the forwarded PostgreSQL port stalls there, so DATABASE_URL uses 127.0.0.1 (local .env.local and .env.example). The earlier P1 trial database was renamed civic_lens_p1_trial_superseded (not deleted) when migrations were corrected; it can be dropped by the user. P3: after the Podman machine restarted the DB container was 'Exited' and had to be restarted with 'podman compose --env-file .env.local up -d db' using the environment above; the CP-00 data in the mcl_pg volume was intact.

openapi.yaml declares X-Demo-Persona as an apiKey scheme without an enum. P2 uses the six non-system values of LifecycleEvent.actorRole (public, citizen, authority, moderator, independent_reviewer, demo_admin), pinned by a drift test. The frozen P1 contract was not edited; a Master Director decision is needed on whether a later contract revision should state the header enum explicitly.

No controlling file defines URL paths for PAGE-01..PAGE-12 (wireframes/pages.json has ids and names only). P2 derives /page-01..../page-12 mechanically from the page id and redirects / to /page-01. Later phases or the Master Director may replace the scheme; apps/web/src/routes.ts is the single place to change.

The persona and language selections are held in memory only and reset on reload, because no controlling P2 file permits browser persistence. Reload persistence needs an explicit decision before any localStorage use.

P2 accessibility and responsive evidence is limited: Vitest runs in Node (react-dom/server) with no jsdom, Testing Library, axe or Playwright installed, so interactive behaviour was checked once by hand in the app's built-in browser at 390x844, 768x1024 and 1440x900 (no horizontal overflow on all 12 pages, 44px targets, skip link, focus move, persona persistence across navigation), and forced-colors rendering was not verified in a browser. Full axe serious/critical and journey gates remain P8 work and are not claimed.

Hindi (hi) and Marathi (mr) bundles are bounded starter translations of the banner, navigation, persona lens and status badges, written without native-speaker review; all other keys fall back to English. Not a full localization.

The API runtime identity is a separate login role. mcl_app stays NOLOGIN because the accepted P1 tests assert it and pin the three-migration list, so P3 added an unprivileged login role mcl_api (member of mcl_app WITH INHERIT FALSE, SET TRUE; every connection runs SET ROLE mcl_app in a read-only session) created by the owner-authority command 'mcl-seed provision-api-role' rather than by a migration (roles are cluster-wide and the password is machine-specific). A fresh machine must run that command with APP_DATABASE_URL in the ignored .env.local. mcl_app still holds the P1 INSERT/UPDATE grants that P3 does not use; they were not revoked because later phases need them, and the P3 session is read-only. Master Director decision needed on whether a later phase should convert this into a migration-managed role.

Contract silence handled by P3 decisions, OpenAPI unchanged: (1) healthReady documents only 200 and 400, so a failed readiness returns 503 with the HealthReady body NOT_READY/DOWN; (2) the contract does not say how ward, category, status and dlpOnly apply to ASSET and PUBLIC_WORK map features, so P3 applies category/status to issues only, derives ward from the asset or issue ward candidate, takes dlpActive from the linked work order (assets: any DLP-active work on the asset) and draws a public work on its asset's geometry; (3) MapFeatureProperties.status is a free string. Needs Master Director confirmation or a contract revision.

Basemap tiles are OpenStreetMap raster tiles from tile.openstreetmap.org, an external service. Their use rests on the non-controlling v1.2.2 guide and is not forbidden by GUARDRAILS.md (no street imagery). Attribution and a strict-origin-when-cross-origin referrer are set, but behaviour behind the corporate TLS-inspecting proxy, OSM tile-policy compliance and offline operation are unproven. Degradation is bounded (one latched notice, synthetic orientation grid, vector features unaffected) and was exercised in one real-browser run with a CSP that blocked the tile host; real tile loading was observed once on the dev server.

PAGE-01 accessibility and responsive evidence is manual and single-run in the built-in browser at 390x844, 768x1024 and 1440x900 (no horizontal overflow, 44px targets except the native checkbox inside a 48px label, keyboard selection by Return on a focused marker, focus outlines, skip link, live-region announcements). Not run: axe, Playwright, forced-colors, prefers-reduced-motion, screen readers, touch. The map exposes 12 keyboard tab stops (mitigated by a skip-to-list link), vector features are 3-8 px at city zoom (the list is the reliable selection route), the wireframe's mobile bottom sheet is simplified to a panel below the active view and the desktop filter rail is a horizontal bar. Leaflet DOM behaviour has no automated test because Vitest runs in Node without jsdom. Does not satisfy P-13 or the P8 accessibility gate.

Production DLP status is evaluated at the wall-clock UTC instant (one instant per request; injectable clock for tests only). The seeded DLP window ends 2027-03-31T18:29:59Z, so the demo's dlpActive and dlpOnly results change after that date and before 2026-04-01. A fixed demonstration instant would need a Master Director decision and a contract-level mechanism (no public evaluationTime parameter was added).

The two read endpoints reject empty, repeated (multiple-value) and unknown query parameters with a 400 problem, which is stricter than the contract text (it declares single scalars and is silent on unknown names). Ward filter options in PAGE-01 are the three codes frozen in DECISIONS.md (K/W, G/N, M/E) because no ward-list operation exists; ward display names and ids are not accepted as filter values.
All new PAGE-01 strings (keys p1.*) exist in English only; Hindi and Marathi fall back to English, extending P2-F05. No native-speaker review has been done.

PostgreSQL development port is published beyond loopback in compose configuration. Evidence (P4, 2026-11-21): compose.yaml maps ports ["5432:5432"] with no host IP (not changed); `podman port` reports 0.0.0.0:5432 and :::5432; Get-NetTCPConnection shows LISTEN on 0.0.0.0, :: , 127.0.0.1 and ::1 for port 5432 owned by a host-side forwarding process (dllhost); a loopback connection test succeeds, and a connection to the host's own Wi-Fi LAN address on 5432 also succeeds from the same machine. This proves the listener is bound to all interfaces on the host. It does NOT prove reachability from another machine: no off-host connection was attempted, the host is on a domain-authenticated network profile, and the firewall inbound rules were not exhaustively resolved (a bounded rule scan matched no 5432-specific allow rule; Windows Firewall default inbound action is NotConfigured). Classified MEDIUM, not HIGH, because external reachability is unproven; it would be HIGH if an off-host probe or a firewall review shows the port is reachable. A controlled hardening test (publish as 127.0.0.1:5432:5432 in a copy of the compose file, restart, confirm only loopback listens, rerun mcl-seed verify) is required and was not done because P4 forbids changing compose.yaml. Credentials are strong local secrets from the ignored .env.local, which limits but does not remove the exposure.

NON-BLOCKING. Local Mumbai offline-basemap source packages (about 272 MB, formerly maps/: Bombay.osm.pbf, GeoJSON, GeoPackage, Shapefile, Parquet, CSV, Garmin and Shortbread/other MBTiles candidates) are available but not yet validated for format, licence, provenance, performance or CivicMapAdapter compatibility. They are treated as UNVERIFIED SOURCE PACKAGES. The packages were moved out of the repository root to C:\Projects\Mumbai Civic Lens\external-inputs\geospatial\osm-bombay (see CON-P4-001, RESOLVED); they are not tracked, not manifested, not committed, and nothing in P4 reads them. No Pyrosm, native GIS dependency, tile server, MBTiles/PMTiles plugin, MapLibre, ArcGIS runtime or service worker was added. Recommended follow-up GEO-01 after P4: a bounded K/West offline-basemap feasibility gate that uses the existing Bombay.osm.pbf with Pyrosm (as a candidate tool only, in an isolated environment), ArcGIS Pro for inspection, and compares bounded GeoJSON, local raster MBTiles and Shortbread vector MBTiles for ODbL attribution, size, load time and CivicMapAdapter fit. Until then P3-F03 stays open and the online OSM layer stays optional.

Contract coverage for PAGE-02/PAGE-03. (a) GET /v1/issues/{id} (getIssue) and GET /v1/audit/{entityId} (getAuditTimeline) are NOT implemented: the Kundali response already carries the full issue and an ordered bounded audit preview, so neither was strictly necessary and P4 does not add routes by existence in OpenAPI; both stay deferred and return 404 (tested). The full audit timeline and correction comparison views are therefore not on PAGE-02; the page shows the committed preview only and says the full view is planned. (b) The Kundali contract has no field for the QR concept beyond canonicalDemoPath, and no page specification requires a QR in P4, so the work-site QR concept is deferred (no QR rendered, no external QR service). (c) The Kundali does not carry a ward boundary geometry for display; none is drawn or invented. (d) PAGE-02 has no ticket-history or ATR attachment beyond the committed claim fields. Display of every other field is supported by committed schema fields; nothing was fabricated.

PAGE-02/PAGE-03 verification is manual single-run browser evidence plus Node react-dom/server unit tests on contract-shaped fixtures (not live proof) plus a live Python OpenAPI-schema verifier; there is no Playwright, axe, screen-reader, forced-colours or reduced-motion run. The six Playwright journey specs remain placeholders (P-13 OPEN). No WCAG conformance is claimed.

DLP status is derived at the request's wall-clock UTC instant, so the Journey 1 dossier changes after the seeded DLP window ends (2027-03-31T18:29:59Z); tests inject a fixed instant (extends P3-F05). The three synthetic evidence illustrations are generic schematic drawings selected only by the committed evidence stage; they are not derived from the fixture media references (fixtures/evidence/*.svg do not exist in the package) and must not be read as depicting the recorded event.

One P3 integration test (dlp_is_derived_from_one_injected_instant_per_request in crates/api/tests/p3_api.rs) failed once in a full `cargo test --workspace` run and passed on every rerun, including the final full run and a targeted run. Cause not established (suspected timing with the concurrently running API process holding the shared test database during a pool/statement-timeout window); not reproduced, not modified. Recorded rather than hidden; to be investigated in a later phase.

Contract ordering: checkDuplicates needs an existing issue id in its path, so submitIssue persists the report (SUBMITTED_UNVERIFIED) BEFORE PAGE-05 shows the duplicate review, and no committed operation links or merges two reports. After Endorse or Add evidence the citizen's own report therefore remains a separate unverified record (PAGE-06 says so; nothing is merged and nothing is rejected). Resolving it needs a product decision or contract change (a pre-submission check or a link operation), which P5 may not add.

The duplicate decision rides addEvidence (duplicateChoice is a member of AddEvidencePayload and evidence metadata is mandatory), so an endorsement is recorded as a citizen fixture-evidence note plus a lifecycle event on the chosen issue; there is no endorsement entity. addEvidence is also absent from traceability/journeys.json J2 operationIds (submitIssue, checkDuplicates, getKundali) although the master guide assigns /evidence to P5; that frozen file was not edited.

Policy gaps, not invented around: considerCarriagewaySide is true for POTHOLE but no carriageway-side data exists in the schemas or seeds, so it is not applied; DRAIN_BLOCKAGE and FACILITY_REPAIR have no committed radius or window, so they earn no radius or window points and are candidates only by sharing the subject's asset; the committed policy file defines no tie rule beyond the ordering used (score descending, then issue id ascending).

DuplicateCandidate (additionalProperties false) has no distance field and DuplicateCandidates carries only policyLabel, so PAGE-05 cannot show the PostGIS-measured metres or a policy version string; the measured distance (about 9.513 m for KND-001 against KND-002) is proven in the SQL tests only.

PAGE-04 collects a Point as coordinates (with a demonstration-location shortcut); there is no map pick, and line or polygon reporting (R-02) is accepted by the API but not offered in the form. The basemap is deliberately not required to report.

Identifiers created by P5 are derived from the scoped Idempotency-Key (SYN-DEMO-KND-R<8 hex>, SYN-DEMO-EVD-R<8 hex>) because idempotency_records holds only key, operation and a hash and the migrations are frozen; reopening PAGE-05 after a refresh re-runs the idempotent check under a new key and appends another DUPLICATE_CHECK_EVALUATED audit event (the result is identical). Sequential ids or event de-duplication would need a schema change.

Intermittent transient database connection failures were seen twice in the P3 and P1 database tests during P5 (the P3 dlp test and the P1 dlp-status test failed once each, then passed on rerun and in every later full run); not diagnosed. Parallel test servers each open their own pools against role connection limits and may be the cause.

The command path answers 503 when the command identity or database is unavailable; the contract documents no 503 for submitIssue, checkDuplicates or addEvidence (same class as P3 readiness). P5 browser checks were manual, not Playwright or axe (P-13 stays OPEN).

Column-level UPDATE grants bound which columns the command identity may change, not which rows or values. The database cannot enforce recordVersion, the JURISDICTION machine or the unlinked-issue rule for that identity; those rules live in crates/infrastructure/src/command.rs (resolve_jurisdiction, link_work), are re-checked by each UPDATE's WHERE clause (zero rows updated is a conflict) and are covered by crates/api/tests/p6_api.rs and tests/p6/verify_live.py. A stronger guard would be BEFORE UPDATE triggers on jurisdictions and issues in a new migration 0004 (0001 to 0003 stay untouched); not added because it needs an owner decision. The grants are: UPDATE (status, external_agency_label, confirmation_basis, confidence_note, record_version, updated_at) ON jurisdictions and UPDATE (work_order_id, record_version, updated_at) ON issues, plus SELECT on work_orders; no other UPDATE, no DELETE or TRUNCATE, nothing on lifecycle_events or corrections.

The effective rationale limit is narrower than the contract's 400 characters. A rationale is stored verbatim in the 400-character lifecycle event summary together with fixed wording, so one that does not fit is refused with 422 (naming how many characters over) instead of being truncated; confirming a ward also stores it as the 300-character confirmationBasis. OpenAPI maxLength is unchanged. Example: a 300-character rationale is refused for an external-agency assignment.

No committed state machine names an event for linkWork: the ISSUE and WORK machines have no work-link transition. P6 appends ISSUE_WORK_LINKED to the issue's chain, changes only issues.work_order_id, record_version and updated_at, and leaves the issue status and the work order untouched. An authority decision is needed on the event name and on whether linking should also move the WORK machine (for example DEFECT_NOTIFIED).

The accusation screen on authority rationales is a bounded English keyword list (ACCUSATORY_STEMS in crates/application/src/commands.rs) with the defined term 'liability period' exempted. It is a guardrail, not moderation: Hindi and Marathi text and paraphrase are not screened, and a legitimate sentence containing a listed stem is refused with fixed wording.

Authority queues are bounded and silent: each list is capped at AUTHORITY_QUEUE_LIMIT (500) with no truncation indicator because the contract has no field for one, and a DLP exception whose dlp_status has a NULL fresh-repair estimate is omitted because DlpExceptionItem requires an integer estimate and none is fabricated. Neither situation occurs in the synthetic data.

getAuthorityDashboard has no queue for jurisdictions assigned to an external agency and awaiting a handoff: uncertainJurisdictionIssueIds covers UNKNOWN, spatially inferred (provisional) and disputed only, and the contract defines no other list. PAGE-08 therefore cannot list assigned-but-not-handed-off items; the authority opens each issue.

X-Demo-Persona is self-asserted. The authority endpoints answer 401 (missing or unrecognised persona) and 403 (any other persona) as a simulated workflow gate, and any local client that sends 'authority' may call them. They are protected only by the loopback bind and the exact-origin CORS list; CAP0-F09 (database port published beyond loopback) remains OPEN. This is not production authentication and must not be exposed publicly.

Idempotent replay returns the current record rather than the original response: idempotency_records stores only a key hash and a request fingerprint, so a replay after a later change returns the newer state and skips the stale-version check. Same schema limit as P5-F06, but P6 creates no key-derived identifiers; lifecycle event ids come from the entity's chain sequence.

P6 browser checks (PAGE-08, PAGE-09 and PAGE-10 at 390x844, 768x1024 and 1440x900; Journey 3 linkage and the first Journey 4 step completed through the UI as the Authority persona) were manual in the built-in browser and are not Playwright or axe coverage; P-13 stays OPEN. The P1 Python contract tests (tests/p1) were not executed in this session because openapi-spec-validator is not installed in the host Python; no contract, schema or seed file was changed.

PAGE-10 implements only the DLP exception view (AUTH-009). The completion-claim half (AUTH-007, claimCompletion) belongs to P7 under the TASKS.md gate order and is shown as an honest not-in-this-phase notice, not faked.
Real journey tests require implementation
Fresh independent Opus audit pending
